title: iTutorGroup automated age-based applicant rejection
system_purpose: Filter applications for remote online tutoring roles using configured eligibility rules
decision_impact: Automatic rejection prevented applicants from advancing to any human review stage
verified_facts: EEOC filed suit alleging that iTutorGroup configured software to automatically reject women aged 55 or older and men aged 60 or older applying for online tutoring positions.
reported_harm: Age and sex-based discriminatory opportunity loss — qualified candidates were rejected without human review or appeal path
quantitative_evidence: More than 200 qualified applicants were automatically rejected; settlement amount was $365000.
limitations: Public source is a settlement announcement and EEOC testimony; no independent technical audit of the software has been published. Testimony explicitly cautions the system may have been rule-based automation rather than machine-learning AI.

title: Amazon experimental ML recruiting tool gender bias
system_purpose: Rank job applicants from resumes to identify top candidates for technical roles
decision_impact: Model recommendations could have influenced which candidates received recruiter attention during internal testing
verified_facts: EEOC-hosted testimony recounts that Amazon developed a recruiting tool from approximately 2014, identified that it penalized resumes containing the word 'women's' and downgraded graduates of all-women's colleges, then scrapped the tool before deployment.
reported_harm: Potential systematic discriminatory opportunity loss against women applicants in technical hiring
quantitative_evidence: The cited testimony provides dates and describes the finding of gender bias but documents no deployed-decision count or measurable affected-applicant rate.
limitations: This was a reported experimental prototype never deployed for actual hiring decisions; the claim derives from press reporting cited in testimony rather than a regulatory adjudicative finding. No technical audit is public.

title: HireVue AI video interview scoring discontinued
system_purpose: Score facial expressions and speech patterns in recorded video interviews to predict candidate suitability
decision_impact: AI score provided to hiring managers alongside interview content; influence on final decision varied by employer
verified_facts: HireVue publicly announced in 2021 that it had removed the facial-expression analysis component of its video interview product following criticism from AI ethics researchers and civil society groups about validity and potential bias.
reported_harm: Potential discrimination by proxy — facial expression scoring may disadvantage candidates with certain disabilities or non-standard speech patterns; scientific validity of personality-from-video inference contested
quantitative_evidence: HireVue stated the facial-expression feature represented less than 10% of the overall score weighting; no independent audit of disparate impact across demographic groups has been made public.
limitations: No regulatory finding of discrimination exists for HireVue video scoring. The company's self-reported weighting and the absence of a public disparate-impact audit make it impossible to verify the actual harm magnitude from public sources.
